metadata.overview: Controls and monitors Schneider Electric PM8000 series smart power meters installed per mining rack. Telemetry covers grid-side voltage, current, real power, power factor, cumulative energy, and frequency. Provides load-shedding capability via circuit breaker control. Power factor below 0.90 indicates reactive load problems — investigate PSU health on the rack.

telemetry.name: voltage_v
telemetry.description: RMS line voltage. Nominal is 230V (EU) or 240V (US). Above 250V is an overvoltage condition — PSUs may clamp or shut down. Below 200V is undervoltage — hashrate drops and PSUs may fault.

telemetry.name: current_a
telemetry.description: RMS current draw for the rack. A sudden drop to 0 while circuit_enabled=true indicates a tripped breaker or PSU failure.

telemetry.name: power_kw
telemetry.description: Active real power consumed by the rack. Calculated as voltage_v × current_a × power_factor / 1000. Alert when this approaches the configured alert_threshold_kw.

telemetry.name: power_factor
telemetry.description: Power factor (0.0–1.0). Ideal is above 0.95 for modern PSUs. Below 0.90 indicates reactive load — may signal aging or failing PSUs on the rack.

telemetry.name: energy_kwh
telemetry.description: Cumulative energy consumed since last counter reset. Used for cost accounting and efficiency trending.

telemetry.name: frequency_hz
telemetry.description: Grid frequency. Nominal 50 Hz (EU) or 60 Hz (US). Deviations beyond ±0.5 Hz may indicate grid instability — log and alert, do not issue commands during instability.

telemetry.name: circuit_enabled
telemetry.description: True when the rack circuit breaker is closed (power flowing). False means load shed or manual lockout. Never enable a circuit without confirming the rack is ready — sudden inrush can trip upstream breakers.

telemetry.name: alert_threshold_kw
telemetry.description: Configured alert threshold for real power. When power_kw exceeds this value, alert.threshold_exceeded is raised. Adjustable via setAlertThreshold command.

commands.name: setCircuitBreaker
commands.description: Opens (false) or closes (true) the rack circuit breaker for controlled load shedding or restoration. Disabling cuts all power to the rack instantly.
commands.constraints: Never disable a circuit without operator confirmation. Re-enabling a circuit causes a high inrush current — stagger enables across racks by at least 5 seconds. Do not toggle a circuit more than 3 times within 60 seconds.

params.name: enabled
params.description: true = close breaker (power on), false = open breaker (power off)

commands.name: resetEnergyCounter
commands.description: Resets the energy_kwh cumulative counter to zero. Used at billing period boundaries.
commands.constraints: This action is irreversible. Only issue at a billing period boundary or after explicit operator confirmation.

commands.name: setAlertThreshold
commands.description: Updates the power threshold (kW) above which alert.threshold_exceeded is raised. Useful for proactive load management.

troubleshooting: alert.overvoltage: If voltage_v > 250V, notify your grid operator immediately. Do not issue other commands — protect hardware by disabling non-critical racks via setCircuitBreaker.
alert.threshold_exceeded: Reduce load by disabling lower-priority racks via setCircuitBreaker or by issuing setPowerLimit to individual miners on the rack.
alert.low_power_factor: power_factor < 0.90 suggests failing PSUs. Schedule PSU inspection during next maintenance window. Do not reset the energy counter until investigation is complete.
alert.circuit_open: If circuit_enabled=false was not intentional, check for a tripped upstream breaker. Restore only after physical inspection confirms rack is safe.

errors.E_OVERVOLT: Grid voltage exceeded safe upper bound — protect connected hardware
errors.E_UNDERVOLT: Grid voltage below safe lower bound — PSUs may fault
errors.E_OVERCURRENT: Current exceeded breaker rating — load shed or breaker trip likely
errors.E_LOW_PF: Power factor below 0.90 — reactive load problem on rack PSUs
